{
  "rules": [
    "When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or shift downward.",
    "After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward after 3–5 days.",
    "If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model overreacts; apply downward bias correction proportional to deviation from recent mean.",
    "When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and price is trending up, model often over-optimistic; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% if sentiment >0.3.",
    "If model forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows early divergence (e.g., first 3–5 days), adjust downward by 2–3% per day to account for lag.",
    "In high-sentiment periods (≥0.4), model tends to overpredict; apply a 5–10% downward adjustment if sentiment >0.4 and price >85.",
    "If true outcome shows a sharp reversal after a peak, model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 5–10% after 2–3 days of upward momentum."
  ]
}
